title: Images and Multimedia
subtitle: Images, image attributes, audio, video and accessible media content.
description: Add visual and multimedia content to your webpages correctly.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 4: Images and Multimedia. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Images and Multimedia”. The goal is to images, image attributes, audio, video and accessible media content.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

Media elements need accurate source paths and suitable fallback behavior. Images should have alternative text that communicates their purpose; decorative images can use an empty alt value so screen readers do not announce irrelevant details.

Practice direction: Open Home → Menu → Practical/Practice → select HTML. Paste this snippet into the matching web/React editor, run or preview it, and compare what happens. Then change one value or element and run it again so you can observe the effect. If this course is not available in the in-app runner, use a suitable compiler or interpreter for the language.

blocks.question: A meaningful chart image conveys weekly progress. What should its alt text provide?
options: A useful text equivalent of the chart’s key information.
Nothing even when the chart matters.
blocks.explanation: Alt text should communicate the relevant purpose or information rather than the file name.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Alt text should communicate the relevant purpose or information rather than the file name.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Alt text should communicate the relevant purpose or information rather than the file name.

blocks.question: A video contains spoken instructions. Which addition helps people who cannot hear the audio?
options: A second copy of the same video.
blocks.explanation: Captions or transcripts make spoken information available in text.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.

blocks.text: Audio and video controls should be provided when users need to play, pause, or adjust playback. Do not autoplay sound unexpectedly, and provide captions or transcripts when spoken or meaningful audio content needs an accessible equivalent.

blocks.question: A program repeatedly looks up a learner by a unique email address. Which structure is a natural fit?
options: A map/dictionary keyed by email, with suitable uniqueness handling.
A random number with no mapping.
A paragraph of comma-separated values that is never parsed.
A loop that guesses the correct person.
blocks.explanation: Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
